minutes.headline: Commission continued the Hickory Hills lake plan, ordered a mitigation redo on Fire Road, and moved to restore the 205 Sunset dock.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission, with new administrator Nadia Madden at her first meeting, approved a replanting plan at 190 Peninsula Drive and issued a negative determination with a wall-removal stipulation at Townsend Harbor Road. It continued the Hickory Hills whole-lake management plan, the marijuana retail NOI at Sumner Street and others, and sent the 16 Fire Road engineer back to modify the berm and tree plan. It voted 3-2 to issue a certificate of compliance for the Pleasant Street bridge over a safety-gap objection.

public_comment.topic: Thanked departing agent Matt Morrow, objected to a driveway decision on Townsend Harbor Road, and promoted a 6/10 candlelight vigil and resolution against violence.

budget_items.topic: Hickory Hills notice and mailing costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said mailing notices to abutters for a new filing took many volunteers and cost real money, arguing a fresh NOI for every spot herbicide treatment would be a financial burden.
The applicant offered replanting as a compensatory measure for the oversized dock.
The grant funds will be fully spent on trail map signs, but the work won't be complete; timber rides fund money will be needed to finish installation.
A member referred to the applicant's stake in the dispute in passing as a large sum.

decisions.decision: Administrator to ask the Fitchburg Land applicant to have Graves Engineering review the project for wetlands bylaw issues, not just planning board.
Chair directed the 16 Fire Road engineer to return with a plan raising the berm to full height and adding trees.
Commissioners agreed to a site visit at 205 Sunset before deciding the enforcement; decision deferred to next meeting.
An enforcement order will be pursued at 411 Goodwin Street after the positive determination.
Administrator asked to inspect a structure in the 30-foot no-disturbance zone at 23 Cove Road and report back.
Commission to ask the new DPW director to help identify a contractor to develop bid specs for window and insulation work at Hollis Road.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted 3-2 to issue a certificate of compliance for the Pleasant Street bridge.
The Commission continued the Hickory Hills whole-lake management plan to June 15.
The chair directed the engineer for 16 Fire Road to return with a plan raising the berm to full height and adding trees.
Commissioners agreed to a site visit at 205 Sunset before deciding on enforcement over the dock, and deferred the decision to the next meeting.
The Commission approved a replanting plan at 190 Peninsula Drive and issued a negative determination, with a wall-removal stipulation, at Townsend Harbor Road.

why_it_matters: Wetlands rulings decide what can be built or kept near water, and the Hickory Hills plan and the Fire Road and Sunset Lane enforcement cases remain unresolved, so the outcomes affect lakefront and wetland property owners.
The Hickory Hills applicant said new abutter notices for each herbicide treatment cost volunteers time and money, so the filing rule the Commission sets will decide who pays for lake treatment.
watch_next: The June 15 meeting, where the Hickory Hills plan, the Fahlula Road warehouse and the 205 Sunset Lane RDA are due to return.
The Commission's decision on enforcement at 205 Sunset after the site visit.
